title: The AML/CFT Framework and Risk-Based Supervision
summary: The international foundations of AML/CFT supervision, the FATF Recommendations and mutual evaluations, and how authorities apply a risk-based approach to their populations of firms.
topic: Reducing Financial Crime & Delivering Market Integrity
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The international foundations of AML/CFT supervision, the FATF Recommendations and mutual evaluations, and how authorities apply a risk-based approach to their populations of firms.
Learning Objectives: Explain the FATF standards and the supervisor's role within the national AML/CFT system
Apply a risk-based approach to supervisory planning and resourcing
Describe how mutual evaluations assess supervisory effectiveness
Syllabus: FATF Recommendations, immediate outcomes and mutual evaluations
National risk assessment, sector risk assessment and firm risk scoring
Roles of the supervisor, the national FIU and law enforcement
Regional AML frameworks and the move to supranational supervision
Intended Audience: AML/CFT, sanctions and financial crime supervisors and inspectors
Market surveillance, conduct and data analytics staff working on financial crime risk
Senior managers shaping the authority's financial crime strategy and use of SupTech
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT, sanctions or conduct supervision is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
